memos.headline: Momentum Leaders AAPL, NVDA, GOOGL, UNH Extended; PG and JPM in Clear Downtrends
memos.body: I see a sharply bifurcated tape today. AAPL is printing a new 52-week high with RSI at 75.7 and sitting 12.8% above its 50-day mean—strong trend but stretched, so I'd wait for a pullback toward the 50d before adding. NVDA (+19.9% over 12w, RSI 64.7) and CAT (+55.9% over 26w, RSI 58.0) show the best combination of momentum and room to run before overbought readings, with strong relative strength vs SPY. On the weak side, PG is in a persistent downtrend—16.7% off its 52-week high, below both moving averages, RSI 41, and relative strength vs SPY of -18.7% over 12 weeks—making it a clear avoid. JPM is similarly weak with negative 4w and 12w returns, trading below both moving averages, and underperforming SPY by 11.3% over 12 weeks. UNH has the strongest relative strength in the universe (+27.9% vs SPY over 12w) but RSI 76.9 and a 23% premium to both the 50d and 200d averages make chasing it here risky; I'd need a retest of the 50d area before getting involved.

views.note: Strong 12w momentum (+19.9%), RSI 64.7 not yet overbought, and best 12w relative strength vs SPY at +11.9%; would reassess on a close below 195 (roughly the 50d mean area).
Massive 26w return of +55.9% with RSI only 58 and 4w rel strength vs SPY of +7.7%; trend intact above the 50d mean area near 783, a close below that level changes my view.
At a new 52-week high which is bullish, but RSI 75.7 and 12.8% above the 50d mean argue for a pullback before entry; would turn long on a retest near 266-270.
Incredible 12w run of +31% and 19.2% above the 50d mean with RSI 70.2—trend is powerful but extension is extreme; a close below 370 would signal the pullback I'd want to buy.
Strongest relative strength in the universe but RSI 76.9 and 23% above both key moving averages is the most extended name here; too stretched to chase, need a pullback toward 320.
Persistent downtrend: -10.7% over 12w, below both moving averages, RSI 41, and -18.7% relative strength vs SPY over 12w; would reconsider only on a close above 150 reclaiming the 200d.
Below both moving averages, negative returns across all timeframes, RSI 41.5, and -11.3% relative strength vs SPY over 12w; needs to reclaim 305 (50d area) to neutralize the bearish setup.
Still 22.2% off its 52-week high and 8.9% below the 200d mean despite a recent bounce; underperforming SPY over 4w and 12w, would need a close above 445 to turn constructive.
12w return of +28.9% with RSI only 58.6 and outstanding 12w relative strength vs SPY of +20.9%; last week's -3.1% dip looks like a healthy pause, would stop out below 250.
Big 26w gain of +37.9% but 12w relative strength vs SPY is -3.4%, suggesting the move is fading; 9.2% weekly spike could be a blowoff, need to see follow-through above 165 to get involved.

memos.headline: GOOGL and MSFT Lead on Earnings Power; XOM and UNH Flash Cash-Flow Compression Warnings
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between durable, accelerating earnings growers and names where margin erosion is already underway. GOOGL stands out with Q1 revenue up 21.8% YoY, net income up 81.2%, and a 56.9% net margin on only $14.79B of total debt—extraordinary operating leverage. MSFT posted 18.3% revenue growth and a 38.3% net margin with net income up 23.1%, while NVDA's full-year 10-K showed 73.2% revenue growth and a 63.1% net margin on minimal debt of $8.47B, though the data is now nearly three months stale. On the other side, XOM's net income collapsed 45.8% YoY to a 4.9% margin, and UNH grew revenue only 2.0% with net income essentially flat—both signal earnings-power deterioration that I am unwilling to pay for until the trajectory inflects. I would need to see XOM margins stabilize above 7% and UNH revenue reaccelerate above mid-single digits before reconsidering.

views.note: 56.9% net margin with 21.8% revenue growth and 81.2% net income growth on a clean balance sheet is the best earnings-power profile in the universe.
38.3% net margin, 18.3% revenue growth, and 23.1% net income growth with moderate $40.26B debt demonstrate durable, expanding earnings power.
Full-year 63.1% net margin and 73.2% revenue growth are extraordinary, though the 10-K data is nearly three months old and I need the upcoming quarter to confirm sustainability.
Net income surged 76.7% YoY to a 16.7% margin on $181.5B revenue, but $122.6B total debt and capex intensity temper my conviction—margin durability above 15% is the key variable.
22.2% revenue growth and 27.2% net income growth with a 14.6% margin suggest strong cycle positioning, though $36.2B debt relative to revenue warrants monitoring.
16.6% revenue growth and 26.6% margin are solid but $82.7B debt is the highest among tech peers; I need to see services mix continue expanding to get more constructive.
10% revenue growth and 33.1% net margin are respectable for a bank, but the rate cycle outlook and $448.8B debt load limit upside conviction.
Steady 18.5% margin and 7.4% revenue growth are defensive but unexciting; I'd need margin expansion above 20% to upgrade.
Net income down 45.8% YoY to a 4.9% margin is clear cash-flow compression; I stay away until margins recover above 7%.
Revenue growth of just 2.0% and flat net income on $77.9B of debt signals stalling earnings power; need reacceleration before engaging.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 3.75% but Rising Long Yields and Sticky 3.3% CPI Argue for Caution on Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode—the upper bound has sat at 3.75% for three months despite 75 bps of cuts over the prior year, and the labor market is stable with unemployment flat at 4.3%. However, the macro backdrop is turning less friendly: headline CPI is running 3.3% YoY, well above target, and the 10-year yield has surged 55 bps over three months to 4.59%, compressing the 10y-2y spread to just 47 bps. This combination of sticky inflation and rising term premia makes me cautious on long-duration growth equities and constructive on banks (which benefit from a positively sloped curve and stable rates) and energy (an inflation hedge). A CPI print that breaks convincingly below 3% or an unemployment spike above 4.5% would flip my regime call toward renewed easing expectations.

views.note: Stable fed funds, positive 10y-2y spread of 47 bps, and no near-term rate cuts support net interest margins for large banks.
With CPI at 3.3% YoY and the Fed on hold, energy acts as a real-asset inflation hedge in a sticky-price environment.
Staples offer defensive positioning but pricing power may be tested as consumer inflation fatigue builds at 3.3% CPI; bond-proxy valuations pressured by 4.59% 10y.
Rising 10y yields (+55 bps in 3 months) and a paused Fed compress the present value of long-duration growth cash flows; I'd wait for a yield reversal.
Quality balance sheet provides some cushion, but the 55 bps backup in the 10y is a headwind for mega-cap growth multiples.
Recurring revenue is a positive, but duration sensitivity keeps me sidelined until the rate trajectory clarifies.
High capex intensity and long-duration profile make AMZN vulnerable as the 10y pushes toward 4.6% with no Fed easing in sight.
Cyclical bellwether benefits from stable employment at 4.3%, but rising yields and sticky inflation cloud the capex outlook.
Ad revenue is macro-sensitive; stable labor market is supportive but rising real rates cap multiple expansion.
Defensive healthcare cash flows are attractive, but medical cost inflation likely tracks headline CPI at 3.3%, squeezing margins.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: GOOGL and CAT Surged, MSFT Sold Off — Sorting Signal from Noise
memos.body: I am reading the Q1/Q2 2026 earnings-reaction tape across our universe and the most striking sentiment divergences are in GOOGL (+10.0% on results), CAT (+9.9%), and MSFT (-3.9%). GOOGL's massive positive reaction followed by a fresh 8-K on 5/11 suggests the narrative is still building and may not yet be fully priced; I have moderate conviction there. CAT's near-double-digit pop on earnings is the strongest industrial signal I see, but at +9.9% the good news may already be in the stock, so I am more cautious on chasing it. MSFT's -3.9% post-earnings drop combined with a director change filing on 5/14 creates a negative tone overhang that I think persists near-term. UNH's +7.0% earnings pop and subsequent Reg FD disclosure on 5/11 point to a constructive narrative shift worth monitoring, while JPM's muted -0.8% reaction and a flurry of governance filings (bylaws, rights modifications) inject uncertainty without a clear positive catalyst.

views.note: A +10.0% earnings pop and follow-on 8-K suggest a positive narrative shift that may still have room to run.
The +9.9% earnings reaction was powerful but likely front-loaded the good news; I'd wait for a pullback before adding.
A -3.9% post-earnings sell-off plus a director departure filing on 5/14 create a negative sentiment overhang near-term.
The +7.0% earnings reaction and a follow-up Reg FD disclosure suggest improving tone and continued positive momentum.
A solid +3.2% earnings reaction is constructive but not decisive; director turnover adds mild uncertainty.
Flat-to-negative earnings reaction (-0.8%) and multiple governance filings including rights modifications signal unclear sentiment.
A -1.0% earnings reaction is mildly negative but not alarming; no strong directional tone shift evident.
A tepid +0.8% earnings reaction despite multiple pre-earnings Reg FD filings suggests the market had already priced in the news.

memos.headline: Oil at $105 Signals Geopolitical Supply Shock; Policy Uncertainty Falling but Energy Risk Dominates
memos.body: I am focused on the extraordinary 66% three-month surge in WTI to $104.66/bbl, which is the single most important geopolitical signal in today's data set. While the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has dropped 40% over three months to 217 and VIX has compressed to 17.26, the oil move suggests a structural supply disruption—likely sanctions enforcement, OPEC+ discipline, or a conflict-related outage—that overwhelms the calmer tone in credit and equity vol. HY OAS at 2.76% and a flattening 10y-2y spread at 0.47pp tell me credit markets are not yet pricing a recession from the energy shock, but I have low confidence that can persist if crude stays above $100. My key policy trigger: any relaxation of sanctions or SPR release that breaks oil below $90 would materially change my views on energy and downstream cost pressures.

views.note: XOM is the clearest beneficiary of $105 crude; three 8-Ks in two months suggest active capital-allocation or regulatory updates consistent with an energy-security premium.
CAT benefits from infrastructure and energy capex but faces input-cost headwinds from elevated oil; three recent 8-Ks may reflect guidance adjustments, so I stay neutral until clarity emerges.
Elevated fuel and logistics costs from $105 oil directly compress AMZN's fulfillment margins; policy uncertainty decline helps consumer demand but not enough to offset the energy headwind.

No direct NVDA filings in the evidence; export-control risk to China remains a structural overhang, but falling policy uncertainty and VIX suggest no imminent tightening—staying neutral with low conviction.
PG faces petroleum-derived input cost pressure from the oil spike, but its pricing power and defensive profile limit downside; two recent Reg FD filings may address margin guidance.
JPM benefits from energy-sector lending and trading revenue in a volatile oil environment; three 8-Ks and tightening credit spreads support a constructive stance.

Technical shows powerful 12w momentum (+31%) though extension is extreme; sizing reflects high conviction tempered by overbought risk.

plans.changes_my_mind: A weekly close below 783 (50d mean area) would break the uptrend and signal the cycle is turning.
